If any reported deficiencies are not corrected, the application must be rejected under sub-section 33(3)."}],"answer":"**Collective trade mark checklist — identified by the Manual (practice)**

Part 33’s relevant-legislation list identifies these provisions of the **Trade Marks Act 1995** [TMM/Part33/x-relevant-legislation27#1]:

- **s 27** — application: how made.
- **ss 161–167 (Part 15)** — object of the Part; definition of a collective trade mark; application of the Act; application for registration; limitations on rights; assignment; and infringement.
- **s 41** — trade mark not distinguishing the applicant’s goods.

For the **Trade Marks Regulations 1995**, that list identifies **reg 17A.49 — Collective trade marks**. The Manual also places this regulation in its international-application/Madrid Protocol references [TMM/Part33/x-relevant-legislation27#1; TMM/Part60/4/7/4/7/14/1].

**General application and examination checks**

- **Act, s 31:** requires the Registrar to examine and report on compliance with the Act and grounds for rejection [TMA1995/s31].
- **Regulations, reg 4.2:** sets the minimum filing requirements, including identification of the mark, goods/services and applicant, and contact information [TMR1995/r4.2].
- **Manual practice:** also directs attention to **reg 4.8** for reporting non-compliance and **s 33(3)** for rejection where reported deficiencies remain uncorrected [TMM/Part10/x-introduction#1].

**Scope limitation:** the supplied legislative extracts do not contain ss 27, 41 or 161–167, or regs 4.8 and 17A.49; the s 33(3) extract is incomplete. Their inclusion above rests on the Manual’s references, not verification of their full legislative text. The passages therefore support this checklist, but not a complete account of the collective-mark provisions or their exceptions."}
